examples.title: Example 1: Setting Draggable and Droppable Areas
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to set draggable and droppable areas for certain components, such as Image and Text.

examples.title: Example 2: Implementing a Custom Drop Animation
examples.description: In API version 18 and later versions, this example demonstrates how to implement a drop animation by using the custom API executeDropAnimation.

examples.title: Example 3: Obtaining Data Asynchronously Through Drag-and-Drop
examples.description: In API version 15 and later versions, this example shows how to obtain data asynchronously through drag-and-drop by using the startDataLoading API.

examples.title: Example 4: Obtaining the Screen ID for the Drag Event
examples.description: In API version 20 and later versions, this example shows how to obtain the drag event by calling the onDragXXX (not onDragEnd) API and obtain the screen ID by calling the getDisplayId API in the drag event.

examples.title: Example 5: Obtaining the Package Name and Cross-Device Status
examples.description: In API version 20 and later versions, this example shows how to obtain the drag event by calling the onDragXXX API, obtain the package name by calling the getDragSource API in the drag event, and obtain the cross-device status by calling the isRemote API.

examples.title: Example 6: Implementing Hover Detection Support
examples.description: In API version 20 and later versions, this example demonstrates how to register a callback by calling the onDragSpringLoading API and obtain the context (current status and notification sequence) by calling the SpringLoadingContext API.

examples.title: Example 7: Delaying Data Provision from the Drag Source
examples.description: In API version 20 and later versions, this example shows how to call setDataLoadParams in onDragStart to delay data provision and call startDataLoading in onDrop to asynchronously obtain data.
